description:
One thing moving through the pipeline: a change to one project of the monorepo, from request to merge. Runs and merges happen outside the machine; their results come back as events on later wakes. The request names the work (id, project, title, what the person expects in their own words) and nothing the machine holds: tier and criteria come from TRIAGED, sent by a triager who is not the requester, the orchestrator or a worker, and nothing leaves triage before it. Run results come from a worker other than the orchestrator, whose id the harness passes in (orchestrator); every worker that reports a run, succeeded or failed, is recorded (workers), and both ids go to every decision the item opens, so neither can answer as the stand-in. Each criterion is checked by CRITERION_CHECKED from an actor who is neither the orchestrator nor a worker; the stand-in may approve accept only when expectationsMet holds, and a new build clears the checks. A tier, once triage sets it, never goes down: a re-triage after a revise may keep or raise it. Tier 0 still has no plan or accept gate. That is acceptable for now because the tier comes from triage, not from the filer. CI and merge results come only from GitHub wakes, which from-github applies only after GitHub's REST API agrees. The machine checks actor and source kinds, that a ref is there, and that ids differ; who the sessions are is checked afterwards against the platform.

Roles: the item records who played each part, by actor: its requester (REQUEST_RECEIVED), triagers (TRIAGED), workers (RUN_SUCCEEDED, RUN_FAILED), criterion checkers (CRITERION_CHECKED) and stand-in answerers (STAND_IN_ANSWERED on any of its decisions, which the decision reports up as STAND_IN_RECORDED). One actor plays one part on an item: an event whose actor already holds a different role there is refused (holdsAnotherRole), so the triager cannot build, check or answer, a worker cannot triage, check or answer, a checker cannot build or answer, and the stand-in cannot triage, build or check. Each decision the item opens takes the roles as they stand. Roles are held by the worker actors, sessions and agents (harness meta.actors), compared by the whole actor: a subagent is agent <session_id>/<agent_id>, so two subagents of one session are distinct from each other and from their parent session, and the lead's triager, builder and checker subagents can play different parts. The person and GitHub are exempt: they are never recorded or compared. A session id is the platform's: the CLI takes CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID and refuses an --actor session:<id> that differs; for a subagent it takes the agent from the plugin's PreToolUse hook (HARNESS_AGENT) and refuses any --actor session or other agent. harness verify-actors checks every session in the log against the Stop hook's ledger and every agent against the SubagentStart hook's record.

ORCHESTRATOR_STARTED.description: Sent by the harness when an orchestrator starts inside the harness; the same event from outside (any event with an actor) is refused.

STAND_IN_RECORDED.description: Sent by the item's own decision when the stand-in's answer is recorded, naming the answering session; the same event from outside (any event with an actor) is refused.

queued.description: Waiting for the scheduler to give it a slot.

triaging.description: Scope, project, tier and acceptance criteria. The triage run's result is TRIAGED {tier, criteria}, from the triager; the item leaves triage only on it. A revise at the plan gate comes back here, and the tier it already has is a floor: a later triage may raise it, never lower it. A triager's failed run is a worker's run like any other.

TRIAGED.description: Refused from the requester's actor, the orchestrator (or while none is known), every worker on the item and an event with no actor: the tier and the criteria are not set by the party that asked for the work, routes it or does it. The machine compares the ids it is given; who the sessions are is checked afterwards.

Refused when the sender, a session or an agent (harness meta.actors), already holds another role on this item (requester, worker, criterion checker or stand-in answerer): the triager plays no other part. The person and GitHub are exempt. The machine compares the whole actor; harness verify-actors checks sessions against the platform's ledger and agents against the SubagentStart records.
Refused unless tier is 0, 1 or 2, and criteria, when given, is a list of non-empty strings. A missing criteria list is no criteria.

Refused when the item already has a tier and this TRIAGED gives a lower one (or none). A revise sends the plan back to triage, which runs again and may keep or raise the tier but never lower it, so a second triage cannot skip a gate the first one set. The guard reads the previous tier from context, which a revise keeps; an equal or higher tier is taken.

RUN_FAILED.description: Refused when the orchestrator reports the run itself, or no orchestrator is known yet: a run result comes from a worker, an actor other than the orchestrator. The machine compares the ids it is given; that the worker really ran is checked afterwards.

Refused when the sender, a session or an agent (harness meta.actors), already holds another role on this item (requester, triager, criterion checker or stand-in answerer): the triager, a checker or the stand-in cannot build. The person and GitHub are exempt. The machine compares the whole actor; harness verify-actors checks sessions against the platform's ledger and agents against the SubagentStart records.

needsCriteria.description: Triage gave no criteria, so nothing could ever show the work is done: the item waits for the person and nothing proceeds from here. Missing criteria never count as met. It is in the person's inbox while it is here (counted and listed with the decisions that wait on the person), and it gives up its work-in-progress slot on entry (ITEM_PARKED), so other work starts while it waits. BLOCK and UNBLOCKED bring it back here, never to building. The way out is to cancel it; a new request with what done looks like starts again.

DECISION_MADE.description: Sent by the item's own decision when it is decided inside the harness; the same event from outside (any event with an actor) is refused.

building.description: A worker thread builds on its own branch and opens a PR. Every build starts with no criterion checked: a check of an earlier build is not evidence for this one.

RUN_SUCCEEDED.description: Refused when the orchestrator reports the run itself, or no orchestrator is known yet: a run result comes from a worker, an actor other than the orchestrator. The machine compares the ids it is given; that the worker really ran is checked afterwards.

Refused when the sender, a session or an agent (harness meta.actors), already holds another role on this item (requester, triager, criterion checker or stand-in answerer): the triager, a checker or the stand-in cannot build. The person and GitHub are exempt. The machine compares the whole actor; harness verify-actors checks sessions against the platform's ledger and agents against the SubagentStart records.

RUN_FAILED.description: Refused when the orchestrator reports the run itself, or no orchestrator is known yet: a run result comes from a worker, an actor other than the orchestrator. The machine compares the ids it is given; that the worker really ran is checked afterwards.

Refused when the sender, a session or an agent (harness meta.actors), already holds another role on this item (requester, triager, criterion checker or stand-in answerer): the triager, a checker or the stand-in cannot build. The person and GitHub are exempt. The machine compares the whole actor; harness verify-actors checks sessions against the platform's ledger and agents against the SubagentStart records.

verifying.description: CI, spec checks and a reviewer run against the acceptance criteria. The reviewer sends one CRITERION_CHECKED {criterion, verdict, evidence} per criterion; the latest verdict for a criterion counts.

CHECKS_PASSED.description: Refused unless a CI result comes from GitHub: actor github, source github-wake, with the GitHub fact as ref. The machine checks the kinds and that a ref is there; harness from-github sends it only after reading the PR from GitHub's REST API and finding the same result, which the ref names.

CHECKS_FAILED.description: Refused unless a CI result comes from GitHub: actor github, source github-wake, with the GitHub fact as ref. The machine checks the kinds and that a ref is there; harness from-github sends it only after reading the PR from GitHub's REST API and finding the same result, which the ref names.

CRITERION_CHECKED.description: Refused from the orchestrator (or while none is known), every worker on the item and an event with no actor: a criterion is checked by someone who did not do or route the work. The machine compares the ids it is given; who the sessions are is checked afterwards.

Refused when the sender, a session or an agent (harness meta.actors), already holds another role on this item (requester, triager, worker or stand-in answerer): the triager or the stand-in cannot check a criterion. The person and GitHub are exempt. The machine compares the whole actor; harness verify-actors checks sessions against the platform's ledger and agents against the SubagentStart records.
Refused unless criterion is one of the item's criteria, verdict is met, unmet or unclear, and a met verdict carries evidence (a non-empty string).

acceptGate.description: expectationsMet is true only when every criterion's latest CRITERION_CHECKED says met, with evidence, from an actor who is neither the orchestrator nor one of the item's workers now. Unmet, unclear, unchecked or no criteria are not met. The accept decision opens with the answer, and when it is false the stand-in cannot decide it, so the person does.

awaitingAcceptance.description: Evidence against each acceptance criterion: is the work doing what the person expected? A criterion checked now takes the item back through acceptGate, which withdraws this decision and opens a new one with the new answer.

DECISION_MADE.description: Sent by the item's own decision when it is decided inside the harness; the same event from outside (any event with an actor) is refused.

CRITERION_CHECKED.description: Refused from the orchestrator (or while none is known), every worker on the item and an event with no actor: a criterion is checked by someone who did not do or route the work. The machine compares the ids it is given; who the sessions are is checked afterwards.

Refused when the sender, a session or an agent (harness meta.actors), already holds another role on this item (requester, triager, worker or stand-in answerer): the triager or the stand-in cannot check a criterion. The person and GitHub are exempt. The machine compares the whole actor; harness verify-actors checks sessions against the platform's ledger and agents against the SubagentStart records.
Refused unless criterion is one of the item's criteria, verdict is met, unmet or unclear, and a met verdict carries evidence (a non-empty string).

awaitingMergeDecision.description: Merge to main, a one-way door: the person decides and the stand-in recommends, unless the person's live grant names merge and has the one-way-door box (spec decision, grantCovers).

DECISION_MADE.description: Sent by the item's own decision when it is decided inside the harness; the same event from outside (any event with an actor) is refused.

MERGED.description: Refused unless a merge comes from GitHub: actor github, source github-wake, with the GitHub fact as ref. The machine checks the kinds and that a ref is there; harness from-github sends it only after reading the PR from GitHub's REST API and finding the same result, which the ref names.

blocked.description: Waiting on something outside the item (a dependency, a conflict, a failing check). Resumes where it stopped.
